beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute.
beats.got: The rollout dashboard counts access, and that number says nothing about use. We report them as one figure, and I know the dashboard.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: The author's own agentic project died the way our programmes die, with no decision. He says so himself, and that is more honest than I expected.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily. The person who answers for it does not. Clear, and a bit clever.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Each option asks something different of the receiver. Sensible, nothing I'd repeat.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: The competitor is the spreadsheet or the colleague they use today. Obvious once said, and still skipped in every launch I've seen.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before building more. I could do that without an agent.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: Seven bullets. Two of them stay with me.

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: Bring what a real person said, not the plan. That is the only homework I'd actually do.

beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Access and use are different numbers. Our rollouts report the first and call it the second.
Before sharing anything, ask what the other person uses today and what would make them switch. The competitor is their spreadsheet or their colleague.
Whoever answers for the agent can't be copied over with the files, so a plan needs a named owner.

monday.move: Pull the usage figures for one of our earlier tool rollouts, then ask one team lead how they do that job today.
monday.who: One team lead I trust, from the last programme
monday.when: Tuesday, in a regular one-to-one if there's a slot
monday.stop_condition: If they say they never needed the tool, I note it and stop there
monday.blocker: The steering group calendar. Also, I don't run an agent myself, so I'm only borrowing the questions.

misconception.why: The author told a story where his own agentic project ended in the same non-decision as our programmes, and he said so plainly. It's still not evidence that this wave is different from the earlier ones, and nothing here showed me a thing that wasn't possible two years ago. So wait-and-see isn't dead. The module's own point, though, is that the human part is where it stalls, and I believe that.

one_line: Less hype than I feared. The part about access versus use is true, though I kept waiting for the agent to show me something, and it mostly didn't.
